items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: I think that really Trumbau did a lot to enhance him when they were playing together... I don't know of any two musicians that complemented each other so well as they did.

ctx.x: Yeah, and you remember every solo. Pretty near. Very few of them. That's the most fantastic thing. And he remembers Trumbau by solos, too.

Trumbau. Frankie Trumbau, to me, I think that he was really great. I mean, to me, he is very, very underrated. Uh-huh. Even to when he was playing with Bix, Bix was so strong, you see, that he overshadowed anyone and everyone. And, of course, I think that really Trumbau did a lot to enhance him when they were playing together. Uh-huh. Because it seemed as though that Trumbau knew every move that he made. Uh-huh. There was nothing that Bix ever did that you wouldn't hear Trumbau right along with him. And it sounds…
Beautiful, beautiful combination. And I think they originated the so-called chase choruses in some of those numbers where back and forth they would answer each other.
